title: Hygiene Without Utilities
summary: How to maintain sanitation, construct emergency latrines, and wash hands without running water.

sections.heading: Step 1 — Build a Tippy-Tap Handwashing Station
sections.body: Construct a foot-operated handwashing station using a clean plastic jug, some sticks, and rope. Hang the jug from a horizontal branch. Tie a rope from the jug handle to a stick on the ground (pedal). Stepping on the pedal tips the jug to pour water, avoiding hand contact with the container. Use soap or wood ash.
sections.warning: Ensure clean water is used in the tippy-tap and do not touch the nozzle with dirty hands.
sections.image_description: A plastic jug hanging from a frame, tipping as a foot presses a stick pedal

sections.heading: Step 2 — Construct a Cat-Hole or Trench Latrine
sections.body: Locate your latrine at least 200 feet (60 meters) away from camps, paths, and water sources (lakes, rivers, wells). Dig a trench 1 foot wide, 2-3 feet deep, and as long as needed. After each use, cover waste immediately with a layer of soil, lime, or wood ash to accelerate decomposition and prevent flies.
sections.warning: Never locate a latrine uphill from a water source or close to camp sites.
sections.image_description: Cross section of a trench latrine showing layers of waste, ash, and soil

sections.heading: Step 3 — Sanitize Eating and Medical Utensils
sections.body: Clean plates, cups, and cooking pots after every meal. Wash with clean water and biodegradable soap or wood ash (potassium hydroxide in ash acts as a natural cleaner). Boil metal medical tools or eating utensils in boiling water for at least 15-20 minutes to sterilize them.
sections.warning: Do not reuse unwashed utensils, as food residue breeds harmful bacteria rapidly.
sections.image_description: Boiling cutlery in a metal pot over an open flame

sections.heading: Step 4 — Dispose of Trash and Greywater Safely
sections.body: Collect solid organic waste and bury it far from camp to avoid attracting wild animals. For greywater (wash water), dig a small soak pit filled with gravel and sand. Pour greywater through the pit to allow the soil to naturally filter out grease, soap, and food scraps.
sections.warning: Never dump greywater directly into open surface water bodies.
sections.image_description: Water soaking into a gravel-filled pit in the soil

when_to_use: During power outages, natural disasters, or wilderness camping when municipal water and sewage systems are offline.
do_not: Locate waste areas uphill or near drinking water sources
Leave human waste exposed to flies and air
Use unsterilized utensils or tools for medical procedures
Neglect washing hands even when water is scarce (use sanitizers or ash)
sources: International Red Cross Emergency Hygiene Manual
